audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does destroy_account remove both account and storage atomically?
audit_items.state_context: Target is OffchainLabs/prysm (Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch, commit 238d5c07df). Prysm is an Ethereum consensus-layer (beacon chain) client. It does NOT implement EVM execution semantics. Functions destroy_account, _main_trie, _storage_tries are Python execution-specs constructs absent from this Go codebase. Exhaustive grep for destroy_account, _main_trie, _storage_tries, SELFDESTRUCT semantic implementation, EIP-6780 logic, and U256 in all Go source files returned zero results.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The audit item targets destroy_account, _main_trie, and _storage_tries — Python execution-specs abstractions implementing EVM state management with Merkle-Patricia trie storage. These constructs are entirely absent from the target codebase (OffchainLabs/prysm, Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch). A comprehensive grep across all Go source files for destroy_account, _main_trie, _storage_tries, SELFDESTRUCT implementation, and EIP-6780 logic returned zero results. Prysm's role is consensus-layer beacon chain management (beacon state, fork-choice, attestations, sync), not EVM execution. EVM execution is delegated to an external execution client (e.g., go-ethereum) via the Engine API. The beacon chain state managed by Prysm is slot-based (BeaconState proto), not account/storage-trie-based.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No EVM account/storage caches exist in Prysm. Prysm's internal caches relate to beacon block root caching, hot/cold beacon state checkpointing (saveHotStateDB), and forkchoice data structures — none of which map to EVM account or storage trie management.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No EVM account or storage state is managed in this codebase.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No code paths exist in prysm for destroy_account, atomic trie removal, or SELFDESTRUCT processing. Symbolic execution cannot identify counterexamples in a code path that does not exist. The only SLOAD/SSTORE opcode byte references found in the entire codebase are opcode constant arrays in a test transaction generation file (testing/endtoend/components/eth1/transactions.go), which generates EVM bytecode for end-to-end testing of the execution layer — not an implementation of EVM semantics.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No code path exists in prysm through which an attacker could interact with destroy_account or atomic trie removal logic, because these functions are absent. Prysm's P2P and RPC attack surface relates exclusively to beacon chain operations (gossip, block processing, attestation, sync). EVM state management is handled entirely by the execution client, which is a separate process.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. The property under test does not apply to this codebase.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'destroy_account removes both account and storage atomically' cannot be evaluated against Prysm because Prysm contains no implementation of EVM account or storage management. The invariant is defined over Python execution-specs types (State, _main_trie, _storage_tries) that have no counterpart in this Go consensus client.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Not applicable. The property is not implemented in this codebase.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The check targets EVM execution-layer state management (destroy_account, _main_trie, _storage_tries, SELFDESTRUCT/EIP-6780). This functionality is explicitly not implemented in OffchainLabs/prysm, which is a consensus-layer client. No relevant code was found after exhaustive search of the Go source tree. This is a category mismatch between the property specification (Python execution-specs) and the target (Go consensus client).
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target this check against an EVM execution client (e.g., go-ethereum, nethermind, besu) that implements the execution-specs state management functions. Prysm delegates all EVM execution to an external execution client via Engine API.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does destroy_storage handle double-deletion safely?
audit_items.state_context: Target is OffchainLabs/prysm (Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch, commit 238d5c07df). destroy_storage is a Python execution-specs function not present in Prysm Go codebase. No storage trie management functions found in exhaustive grep. KeyError is a Python exception type with no analog in Go.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The audit item targets destroy_storage, a Python execution-specs function responsible for safely removing storage tries without raising KeyError on double deletion. This function and the underlying storage trie management (_storage_tries dict) are entirely absent from the target codebase. A comprehensive search of all Go source files in prysm returned zero matches for destroy_storage, _storage_tries, KeyError (a Python exception class), or any EVM storage trie management code. Prysm interacts with execution layer storage indirectly through the Engine API (engine_client.go), treating execution payloads as opaque blobs.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No EVM storage trie management exists in Prysm. The only storage-related caches in Prysm are for beacon block caching and beacon state hot-state persistence, which are unrelated to EVM account/storage deletion semantics.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No EVM storage deletion code exists in this codebase.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No destroy_storage function or equivalent exists in prysm. There are no code paths to symbolically execute for this property. The double-deletion safety concern (KeyError on second call) is a Python dict semantics concern that has no analog in the Go consensus client codebase.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No entry point in prysm leads to EVM storage trie deletion. Prysm's P2P surface handles LibP2P gossip topics (beacon blocks, attestations, sync committee messages), none of which directly trigger EVM storage deletion. The Engine API client (ForkchoiceUpdated, NewPayload) sends execution payloads to the execution client but does not implement storage deletion internally.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. The property under test does not apply to this codebase.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'destroy_storage must not raise KeyError on double deletion' cannot be evaluated against Prysm. The Python KeyError exception type does not exist in Go, and destroy_storage has no implementation in this codebase. The invariant is entirely scoped to the Python execution-specs implementation.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The check targets destroy_storage (Python execution-specs EVM storage trie deletion). This function does not exist in OffchainLabs/prysm. The concern about KeyError on double deletion is a Python-specific error type inapplicable to Go code. This is a complete category mismatch between the property specification layer and the target codebase.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target against an execution client that implements execution-specs storage management (e.g., py-evm, go-ethereum's EVM storage layer). Prysm has no involvement in EVM storage trie lifecycle management.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does mark_account_created persist across reverts?
audit_items.state_context: Target is OffchainLabs/prysm (Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch, commit 238d5c07df). mark_account_created, created_accounts are Python execution-specs concepts absent from Prysm. Prysm does not implement EIP-2200 gas accounting or SELFDESTRUCT EVM opcode logic. Exhaustive search returned zero results for these terms.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The audit item targets mark_account_created and the created_accounts set in Python execution-specs, which tracks newly created contract addresses to determine EIP-2200 gas refund eligibility and EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT eligibility within a transaction. These constructs are absent from the prysm codebase. An exhaustive search for mark_account_created, created_accounts, EIP-2200, and EIP-6780 in prysm Go source files yielded zero results. Prysm manages beacon state (validators, epoch transitions, fork-choice), not EVM transaction execution context.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No EVM transaction execution context (including created_accounts set) exists in Prysm. Prysm's state management involves BeaconState proto fields (validators, balances, randao mixes, etc.) — none of which relate to contract creation tracking or gas refund accounting.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No EVM transaction execution state is managed in this codebase.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No mark_account_created function or created_accounts set exists in prysm. The property concerns whether a contract-creation marker persists correctly across EVM call-frame reverts — a transaction execution context concern that is entirely absent from Prysm's consensus-layer implementation.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No code path in prysm processes EVM CREATE/CREATE2 opcodes or manages a created_accounts set. The beacon chain processes execution payloads as opaque headers (block hash, state root, receipts root) verified via the Engine API, but does not interpret individual EVM opcodes or track per-transaction contract creation events.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. The property under test does not apply to this codebase.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'mark_account_created must persist across EVM call-frame reverts' cannot be evaluated against Prysm, which contains no EVM call frame management, no created_accounts set, and no EIP-2200 or EIP-6780 implementation. These are execution-layer concerns handled entirely by the external EL client.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The check targets mark_account_created and created_accounts (Python execution-specs EVM transaction context). These concepts do not exist in OffchainLabs/prysm. EIP-2200 gas accounting and EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT eligibility are execution-layer concerns implemented in the EL client, not the CL client. Complete category mismatch.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target against py-evm or another execution-specs-conformant EVM implementation. This check is not applicable to Prysm.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_storage return U256(0) for unset keys?
audit_items.state_context: Target is OffchainLabs/prysm (Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch, commit 238d5c07df). get_storage, U256, SLOAD are EVM execution-layer concepts not present in Prysm. Confirmed: no SLOAD/SSTORE semantic implementations in codebase. Only opcode byte constants (0x54, 0x55) found in a test transaction generator file with no semantic implementation.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The audit item targets get_storage (Python execution-specs SLOAD implementation) and the U256 type, which is a 256-bit unsigned integer used in EVM storage slot semantics. These constructs are entirely absent from the prysm codebase. A comprehensive search for get_storage, U256, SLOAD (as a semantic function — not opcode byte constant), and EVM storage slot access in prysm Go source files returned zero results. The one file containing SLOAD as a byte constant (0x54) is a test transaction generator with no semantic storage implementation.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No EVM storage slot access logic exists in Prysm. The codebase does not implement storage trie lookup, default value semantics for uninitialized keys, or any analog to EVM SLOAD.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No EVM storage access code exists in this codebase.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No get_storage function, U256 type, or SLOAD semantic implementation exists in prysm. The property 'SLOAD of unset key must return U256(0)' is an EVM execution semantics invariant that cannot be evaluated against a consensus-layer client. No counterexample can be constructed from non-existent code.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No attacker entry point in prysm leads to EVM storage slot reads. Prysm processes execution payloads but does not evaluate individual EVM opcodes or access EVM storage slots. Any SLOAD that occurs during EVM execution happens inside the execution client process (accessed via Engine API), not within Prysm.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. The property under test does not apply to this codebase.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'get_storage of unset key returns U256(0)' cannot be evaluated against Prysm. The U256 type and storage slot access semantics are entirely absent from the Go consensus client. This invariant is defined in the Ethereum Yellow Paper and enforced by execution clients, not consensus clients.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The check targets get_storage and U256 default value semantics (Python execution-specs SLOAD implementation). These constructs do not exist in OffchainLabs/prysm. SLOAD semantics are enforced by the execution client. Complete category mismatch between property specification (EVM execution layer) and target (consensus layer).
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target against an EVM execution client (go-ethereum's core/vm/instructions.go opSload, nethermind's EVM storage implementation, or py-evm's get_storage). The SLOAD default-value invariant is properly tested at the execution client level.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does set_storage require account existence?
audit_items.state_context: Target is OffchainLabs/prysm (Go consensus client, fusaka-audit branch, commit 238d5c07df). set_storage, AssertionError for orphaned storage tries are Python execution-specs concepts absent from Prysm. No EVM opcode implementation (SSTORE semantic) found in Prysm. Beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go submits payloads to external EL client but does not implement EVM state management internally.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The audit item targets set_storage (Python execution-specs SSTORE implementation) and the associated assertion that an account must exist before its storage can be written, to prevent orphaned storage tries. These constructs are entirely absent from prysm. A comprehensive search for set_storage, orphaned storage, AssertionError (a Python built-in exception), and SSTORE semantic implementation in prysm Go source files returned zero results. Prysm does not implement SSTORE or any EVM opcode execution semantics.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No EVM account existence verification or storage write logic exists in Prysm. The beacon chain state managed by Prysm contains no concept of EVM accounts or storage tries — its state is beacon-chain-specific (validators, proposers, committees, slashings, deposits).
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable. No EVM account/storage write code exists in this codebase.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No set_storage function, AssertionError guard, or orphaned storage trie concern exists in prysm. The property 'SSTORE must assert account existence to prevent orphaned storage tries' is an EVM execution semantics invariant absent from this consensus-layer codebase. No code paths exist to symbolically execute.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: No attacker entry point in prysm leads to EVM storage writes. Prysm's Engine API client (beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go) submits execution payloads to the execution client but does not perform any EVM state writes internally. All SSTORE processing is handled by the execution client in a separate process.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: None. The property under test does not apply to this codebase.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'set_storage must assert account existence before storage write to prevent orphaned tries' cannot be evaluated against Prysm. The Python AssertionError guard, the _main_trie account lookup, and the _storage_tries dict management are all execution-specs constructs absent from this Go consensus client. Prysm's state consistency is maintained at the beacon state level, not EVM state level.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The check targets set_storage account-existence assertion (Python execution-specs SSTORE guard against orphaned storage tries). This function and the underlying account/storage trie model do not exist in OffchainLabs/prysm. The concern about orphaned storage tries corrupting state is valid for execution clients but completely inapplicable to the consensus client. Complete category mismatch.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Re-target against an EVM execution client that implements execution-specs account/storage trie management. The correct audit targets would be go-ethereum's statedb.SetState with deleted-account check, or py-evm's set_storage implementation with its assertion guard.
